title: PR8061 Staging Gateway Governance Authority Store boundary repair

phases.objective: Preserve the Runtime/Governance database ownership boundary for the Staging Activation Gateway and align the existing schema-role manifest with the governed Staging grant surface, without adding a migration or allowing production/provider mutation.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Build the Staging Activation Gateway rollout plan with distinct Runtime and Governance query executors and validate the existing database-role manifest against the Staging grant contract.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Governance-owned authority bindings and gateway execution tables remain Governance-owned, Runtime excludes those Governance surfaces, required schema tables are already supplied by existing migrations, and no provider or production mutation occurs.
steps: Classify the shared runtime change against canonical environment-impact policy.
Execute the registered Activation Gateway rollout surface regression in dry-run mode.
Verify platform_resource_authority_bindings never reaches the Runtime executor.
Verify workspace_registry remains a Runtime DB read.
Verify a Runtime executor cannot be reused as the Governance Authority Store.
Verify every Governance grant-required table is present in roles.governance.required_tables and excluded from the Runtime role manifest.
Execute the schema-bundle builder regression that requires every Governance table to remain Runtime-excluded.
Require live Staging certification before any governed Staging apply path is considered complete.
assertions: The environment impact declaration source of truth is the canonical deployment branch policy.
Both staging and production are explicitly declared because the changed runtime module is shared, and cross-environment review is explicit.
The Runtime DB does not serve platform_resource_authority_bindings.
The three Staging Activation Gateway execution tables are Governance-required and Runtime-excluded in the role manifest.
The grant policy and schema-role manifest cannot drift without failing regression tests.
No new migration is introduced because the required tables are already created by the existing migration set.
No SQL/GRANT changes, Cloudflare/provider writes, Production deployment, or Production mutation are introduced.
